plan.notes: Official NMSU 2025-2026 Academic Catalog (archived edition), 'Psychology - Bachelor of Arts', A Suggested Plan of Study for Students (Las Cruces campus). The catalog organizes this roadmap by academic YEAR (Freshman/Sophomore/Junior/Senior) with no official semester-by-semester sequence, so it is collected as a single requirements block per convention; courses are listed in catalog year order. Year structure: Freshman Year - ENGL 1110G, MATH choice, PSYC 1110G, PHIL choice, FYEX 1112, COMM 1115G, science choice, first language-series course, Area VI course (29 cr at minimums); Sophomore Year - ENGL choice, Area III/IV course, gened elective, PSYC 2110/2120/2220/2250 core, language-series courses, minor/elective (30 cr); Junior Year - PSYC 3120, PSYC 3110, PSYC upper-division elective, final language-series course, Viewing a Wider World course, upper-division minor/elective courses (27 cr); Senior Year - PSYC 4999 capstone, PSYC upper-division electives, PHIL upper-division elective, Viewing a Wider World course, upper-division minor/elective courses, PHED elective (34 cr). Roadmap assumes placement in MATH 1350G Introduction to Statistics and ENGL 1110G Composition I; not a contract. Choice slots recorded at catalog minimum credit per convention: language-series slots 3-4 recorded at 3, science choice recorded at 4, Area III/IV and gened elective slots 3-4 recorded at 3. PSYC 3110 Experimental Methods is listed as 0-4 credits in the catalog; recorded at 0 and marked required_zero per the variable-credit convention (excluded from sums). Year totals at minimums: 29/30/27/34 = 120, matching 'Total Credits 120-131' at its minimum.
